questions.prompt: What is the big idea of Spiders?
choices: Spiders use their bodies, silk, and senses to survive.
Only tiny spinnerets at its rear make strong, stretchy silk.
Only a web spider feels trapped prey tugging on the silk.
questions.answer: Spiders use their bodies, silk, and senses to survive.
questions.rationale: A spider has eight legs and two body sections—but no wings. How does it catch flying insects? Other spiders make flat sheets, deep funnels, or loose tangles. That garden web may catch insects before they reach the tomatoes. Together, these facts show the whole-book big idea: Spiders use their bodies, silk, and senses to survive.
